title: A Son of Adam
author: Joseph Jacobs
summary: 一个农夫责怪亚当，主人用一桌宴席和一只老鼠让他明白自己也未必能守住规矩。
publicDomainBasis: Published 1894; collected by Joseph Jacobs (1854–1916). Public domain in the United States and in China (author's life plus 70 years).

paragraphs.en: A man was one day working. It was very hot, and he was digging. By-and-by he stopped to rest and wipe his face; and he was very angry to think he had to work so hard only because of Adam's sin. So he complained bitterly, and said some very hard words about Adam.
paragraphs.zh: 一天，一个人正在干活。天气很热，他在挖土。过了一会儿，他停下来休息，擦擦脸；一想到自己得这么辛苦地干活全是因为亚当犯了罪，他就非常生气。于是他狠狠抱怨，说了亚当不少难听的话。

paragraphs.en: It happened that his master heard him, and he asked, "Why do you blame Adam? You'd ha' done just like Adam, if you'd a-been in his place."
paragraphs.zh: 碰巧他的主人听见了，问他：“你为什么要怪亚当？要是你处在他的位置，你也会跟亚当一样。”

paragraphs.en: "No, I shouldn't," said the man; "I should ha' know'd better."
paragraphs.zh: “不，我不会，”那人说，“我会比他更明白事理。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, I'll try you," says his master; "come to me at dinnertime."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我来试试你，”主人说，“午饭时候到我这儿来。”

paragraphs.en: So come dinnertime, the man came, and his master took him into a room where the table was a-set with good things of all sorts. And he said: "Now, you can eat as much as ever you like from any of the dishes on the table; but don't touch the covered dish in the middle till I come back." And with that the master went out of the room and left the man there all by himself.
paragraphs.zh: 到了午饭时间，那人来了。主人把他带进一个房间，桌上摆满了各式各样的好东西。主人说：“现在，桌上的菜你想吃多少就吃多少；但中间那个盖着盖子的盘子，在我回来之前别碰。”说完，主人走出房间，把那人独自留在那里。

paragraphs.en: So the man sat down and helped himself, and ate some o' this dish and some o' that, and enjoyed himself finely. But after awhile, as his master didn't come back, he began to look at the covered dish, and to wonder whatever was in it. And he wondered more and more, and he says to himself, "It must be something very nice. Why shouldn't I just look at it? I won't touch it. There can't be any harm in just peeping." So at last he could hold back no longer, and he lifted up the cover a tiny bit; but he couldn't see anything. Then he lifted it up a bit more, and out popped a mouse. The man tried to catch it; but it ran away and jumped off the table and he ran after it. It ran first into one corner, and then, just as he thought he'd got it, into another, and under the table, and all about the room. And the man made such a clatter, jumping and banging and running round after the mouse, atrying to catch it, that at last his master came in.
paragraphs.zh: 那人坐下来，自己动手吃起来，尝尝这盘，尝尝那盘，吃得很痛快。可过了一会儿，主人还没回来，他便开始盯着那个盖着的盘子，琢磨里面到底是什么。他越想越好奇，自言自语道：“里面一定是什么很好吃的东西。我为什么不能就看一眼呢？我不碰它。只是偷看一眼，不会有什么坏处。”最后，他再也忍不住了，把盖子掀起一点点，但什么也看不见。他又掀起一点，一只老鼠突然跳了出来。那人想抓住它，可它跑掉了，跳下桌子，他便追了上去。老鼠先跑进一个角落，他刚要抓住，它又窜到另一个角落，钻到桌子底下，满屋子乱跑。那人追着老鼠又跳又撞，弄得叮当乱响，最后把主人引了进来。

paragraphs.en: "Ah!" he said; "never you blame Adam again, my man!"
paragraphs.zh: “啊！”主人说，“以后可别再怪亚当了，伙计！”
